title: Recording: George Harrison on New Morning by Bob Dylan | 1970
content:
George Harrison took part in a recording session with Bob Dylan in the afternoon of 1 May 1970.

The session took place in Studio B at the Columbia Records studios at 49 East 52nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Harrison was in the city from 23 April until 5 May.

This was the first New Morning session. Also present were Bob Johnston on piano, Charlie Daniels on bass guitar, and Russ Kunkel on drums. The producer was Johnston.

They performed ten songs: ‘Time Passes Slowly’, ‘Mama, You Been On My Mind’, ‘I Met Him On A Sunday (Ronde-Ronde)’, ‘One Too Many Mornings’, ‘All I Have To Do Is Dream’, ‘Gates Of Eden’, ‘Matchbox’, ‘Your True Love’, ‘It Ain’t Me Babe’, and ‘If Not For You’. The last of those was included in the 1991 box set The Bootleg Series Volumes 1–3.

Snippets of other songs were also recorded, including ‘Sign On The Window’, ‘Working On The Guru’, Went To See The Gypsies’, ‘Song To Woody’, ‘Don’t Think Twice, It’s Alright’, ‘Yesterday’, ‘Just Like Tom Thumb’s Blues’, ‘Da Doo Ron Ron’, ‘Ghost Riders In The Sky’, ‘Cupid’, ‘I Threw It All Away’, ‘I Don’t Believe In You (She Acts Like We Never Have Met)’, ‘Las Vegas Blues’, ‘Fishin’ Blues’, ‘Honey, Just Allow Me One More Chance’, ‘Rainy Day Women #12 & 35’, ‘Tomorrow Is A Long Time’, ‘Cupid’, and ‘Telephone Line’.

The Harrison-Dylan recordings were initially included in a very limited copyright extension release in 2020, Bob Dylan – 50th Anniversary Collection 1970.. Due to public demand they were given a wider release later that year on the Dylan collection 1970.
